overview: Studying Law in Italy allows Indian students to study civil law, international law, European Union law, business law, human rights, and comparative legal systems. Italy has a long legal tradition and universities that offer programs in law, legal studies, international relations and European legal affairs.

Students can choose from Bachelor's and Master's programs in Law in Italy , including the five-year single-cycle degree in Law, international and European law programs and specialized postgraduate courses. The right path depends on whether you want to practice law in Italy, pursue an international legal career, work in corporate compliance or pursue further legal studies in India.

Important: Having a law degree from Italy does not automatically qualify an Indian student to become an advocate in India or a lawyer in Italy. You will need to check professional recognition and licensing requirements separately.

items: Strong legal heritage: Explore the civil-law tradition and its impact on European legal systems.
European legal exposure - explore EU law, international law, human rights and transnational legal issues.
Specialization options: Choose areas like corporate law, international business law, intellectual property or comparative law.
International learning environment: Some universities provide law programs in English.
Research opportunities Develop legal research, analytical reasoning, drafting and argument skills.
Career flexibility: With the right qualifications you will be prepared for opportunities in legal research, compliance, international organizations, business and further legal education.
2. Italian Law Courses
There are different ways for students who want to study Law in Italian universities . It really depends on the legal system you want to study and the career you want to pursue.
Program
Typical length:
Study Areas: Primary
Bachelor of Comparative, European and International Law Studies
3 years
Comparative law, European law, international law, legal systems
Bachelor in Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies
3 yrs
Constitutional law, international law, economics, transnational legal issues
Single-Cycle Law Degree 5 years
Civil law, criminal law, constitutional law, administrative law, legal procedure
Master's degree in Global Law or equivalent specialization
1-2 years (depending on qualification)
International Law, Global Governance, Comparative Law, Transnational Regulation

For example, the University of Trento offers a three-year Bachelor's in Comparative, European and International Legal Studies in English and the University of Turin offers a three-year Bachelor's in Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies in English.
Important distinction: The three-year international or comparative law degree is not the same as the five-year Italian single-cycle Law degree designed for the domestic legal education path.
3. Best Global Universities for Law in Italy
1. University of Trent
Place: Trento

The university offers a Bachelor's in Comparative, European and International Legal Studies taught in English. The program includes comparative legal systems, EU law and international legal perspectives and is therefore relevant to students interested in cross-border legal work and further international studies.
Web site: unitn.it
2. Università di Torino
Site: Turin

Its three-year Bachelor's in Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies is taught in English and covers areas like international law, economics and constitutional law. It is a choice for students interested in legal issues that cross national borders.
Official site: en.unito.it
3. Bologna University
Location: Bologna, Italy

The University offers a five-year single-cycle degree in Law taught in Italian. The curriculum offers a broad legal foundation with opportunities for international study and selected courses in English. Students who are interested in pursuing this path should evaluate their Italian language skills and career goals.
Official website: unibo.it
They are examples of universities with relevant law programs and not a formal ranking. Check the latest course catalog and admission notice for the intake you wish to apply to.

sections.title: Who can study Law in Italy

items: Eligibility for Law in Italy depends on the program and the level of qualification.
For a Bachelors degree:
Passed Class 12 from a recognized board.
A secondary school qualification accepted by the university.
English language skills for English taught programs.
Knowledge of Italian language for courses taught in Italian.
An entrance test or selection (where required)
Master's degree: 1.
A recognized bachelor's degree in Law or other acceptable discipline as determined by the program.
Relevant academic credits or prerequisite subject mentioned.
Knowledge of English or Italian as per the programme's requirements.
CV, letter of motivation, academic references or interview on request.

For instance, the University of Trento's Comparative, European and International Legal Studies program asks for a suitable secondary-school qualification and selection through an admission test. It shows the selection procedure and deadlines applicable for its admission call.
Meeting minimum eligibility requirements is no guaranty of admission. Applicants should check the latest rules and places available.

Some programs are competitive to get on and/or have limited places. Please refer to the university's official application portal for the deadlines, testing arrangements and documentation required for the current intake.
6. Law Study Cost in Italy
Tuition fees for Law in Italy vary depending on the university, program, degree level, and whether you qualify for financial assistance.
Type of institution
Example of annual tuition
Approx. INR value
Public universities €1,000-€4,000

These are planning estimates only and not verified fees for the specific programs listed above. Tuition is subject to change. Do check the official fee schedule from the university for the current fees.
Other costs include accommodation, food, transport, books, insurance, travel and visa costs. Students will have to budget for these separately.
Law Student Scholarships
Indian students can look forward to:
University scholarships are based on merit.
Tuition reductions based on need.
Regional scholarships and awards.
Funding possibilities for international students.
Waivers of fees by the university.
Eligibility, amounts, expenses covered, deadlines all differ. Students must check the university and regional scholarship rules that apply before counting on financial aid.
7. Applying for law in Italy
Your legal path is your choice: Decide whether you want a general Law degree or a specialization in international, European or comparative law.
Shortlist universities: Compare program language, length, curriculum, admission requirements, career outcomes.
Check eligibility: Verify academic qualifications, language proficiency, entrance tests, and application deadlines.
Prepare documents: Gather certificates, transcripts, passport details and motivation letter or CV if required.
Send your application in: Apply on the university's official platform and undergo any admission test or selection procedure.
Get your admission decision: Follow the instructions to accept your offer and complete your enrollment.
Complete visa formalities 1. Follow procedures for Italian student-visa and pre-enrolment, where applicable.
Get ready to enroll: Book accommodation, insurance, travel and any other university requirements.
Deadline varies by university and applicant category. International applicants should begin preparing far ahead.

sections.title: Recognition of Law Degree in Italy

items: Indian students should know the difference between academic recognition and professional qualification when choosing a Law program.
A recognized degree can ease the way to further study or employment in related fields.
A law degree in international or European law does not automatically qualify a graduate to practise domestic law in Italy.
To practice as a lawyer in Italy you may need the proper academic qualifications, practical training, examinations and professional registration under the applicable rules.
Practising as an advocate in India is subject to relevant India legal education and professional recognition requirements.

If you intend to practice in India, you must consult the Bar Council of India (BCI) before enrolling for a foreign law program. Please confirm the exact qualification and institution meets the applicable rules. If you want to practice in Italy, check the current requirements with the relevant Italian authorities and professional bodies.
9. Employment Opportunities and Wages After Law in Italia

Many domestic legal positions require knowledge of the Italian language. Knowledge of English and cross-border legal systems can be useful in international organizations and multinational companies. Employment is conditional upon obtaining all necessary work authorization.

faq.question: Can Indian students study Law course in Italy in English?
faq.answer: Yes. There are programs such as the Comparative, European and International Legal Studies degree of the University of Trento and the Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies degree of the University of Turin.

faq.question: How long is the Law study in Italy?
faq.answer: Some law-related bachelor's degrees in English take three years. The traditional Italian single-cycle Law degree is a five-year program. The length of master's programs differs.

faq.question: Can I practice law in India after studying law in Italy?
faq.answer: Maybe. But it's not automatic. Before choosing your program, you should make sure that the foreign qualification is recognized and meets the Bar Council of India requirements.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study Law in Italy?
faq.answer: Costs depend on the university and on the program. While public colleges may be relatively inexpensive, private colleges can be more expensive. Other costs should be budgeted separately.

faq.question: What are the career opportunities after studying law in Italy?
faq.answer: Depending on the degree and professional requirements, graduates may pursue legal research, corporate compliance, contract management, policy research, international business support or further legal education.
